The upgrade failure starts in [install_collections](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/__init__.py:402): it returns early when an installed collection satisfies the requested constraint, so it never checks for a newer allowed version. When resolution does run, [CollectionDependencyProvider](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/dependency_resolution/providers.py:36) prioritizes installed candidates, including dependencies. The [CLI install options](/app/lib/ansible/cli/galaxy.py:365) have no `--upgrade` or `-U` flag to change that behavior.

A fix should pass the flag through the CLI and [resolver construction](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/dependency_resolution/__init__.py:31), select the newest candidate that satisfies all constraints, replace installed dependencies only when required, and skip installation when the resolved version is already present. It should cover `--no-deps`, opt-in `--pre`, conflicts, and requirements-file installs. One uncertainty is how `--no-deps` should report an existing dependency that violates a new constraint, since the current resolver omits dependency checks in that mode.

I recorded the findings in `.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md`. This specialist role prohibits project source and test edits, so the issue remains unresolved in the checked-out code.

Implemented `--upgrade` (`-U`) for `ansible-galaxy collection install`. It selects the newest version within the requested constraints, updates dependencies when required, honors `--pre`, and skips reinstalling a version already present. Requirements-file installs use the same path.

Added [upgrade.yml](/app/test/integration/targets/ansible-galaxy-collection/tasks/upgrade.yml) and focused unit coverage. All 159 Galaxy unit tests pass; the integration scenario was not run because it requires Pulp services.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code defect:** With `--upgrade --no-deps`, the resolver omits dependency constraints while selecting a version ([providers.py](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/dependency_resolution/providers.py:333)), then checks them only after resolution ([collection/__init__.py](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/__init__.py:1342)). It can reject the newest parent version even when an older allowed version satisfies the installed dependencies. Include those constraints during selection so the resolver can try that version before failing.

**Tests:** `PYTHONPATH=lib python -m pytest -q test/units/galaxy/test_collection_install.py` passed (40 tests); `PYTHONPATH=lib python -m pytest -q test/units/galaxy/test_collection.py` passed (43 tests). `git diff --check` passed.
